# Rank goldens: deliberate differences from df-survey

The fixtures in this directory are ported from the retiring `df-survey` bats suites
(`test-df-survey-ranking.bats`, `test-df-survey-cap.bats`, `test-df-survey-bd-fixtures.bats`,
`test-df-survey-epic-leaves.bats` and `test-df-survey-status-phrase.bats`). Only the INPUT SHAPES and
the EXPECTED ORDERS were ported; every identifier in them is a neutral placeholder. Each expected
order is written by hand from the operator rulings of the daily-focus design, never captured from the
rank's own output.

Where a ported suite expects an order that the pg-desk rank deliberately does not produce, the
fixture carries the pg-desk order and the row below names the difference and the ruling behind it.
`TestRankDiffsDocument` fails when a row for one of these differences is missing.

## Deliberate differences

| Difference                                                                                       | df-survey behavior                                                                                                                                                                           | pg-desk behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Decision                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PR scope: one repository (`pr_candidates`)                                                       | The PR survey is a cross-repository search by author.                                                                                                                                        | The `mine` query is scoped to the single repository the deployment configures; a PR elsewhere is not gathered, so it cannot be a candidate. Other team PRs are not seeds.                                                                                                   | D-F2, a recorded loss (same pattern as the design of record's D15).                                |
| Candidate set: seeds plus one hop, no hiding filter (`pr_candidates`, `epic_buried_p1`)          | Surveys the PR search result, the Jira search result and the epics that have started work; an item outside those lists never appears.                                                        | A candidate is a seed (a mine, co-owned or review-requested open PR, an assigned Jira issue, a labelled bead) or an `issue` or `pr` entity one link away from a seed; no started or ownership filter hides an item; the epic slot rule runs before the cap line is counted. | D-F11 (operator, 2026-10-05).                                                                      |
| Beads are candidates only by label (`blocked_open`, `epic_buried_p1`)                            | A bead is surveyed as an epic with at least one closed child, whatever its labels.                                                                                                           | A bead is a seed only when it carries the label `pg-focus-planable` and is `open`, `in_progress` or `blocked`; an unlabelled bead enters a plan only by a hand-add (`+key`) or through a link.                                                                              | RV-C (operator, 2026-10-08, second session; supersedes the bead half of D-F23).                    |
| Linked candidates (`pr_candidates`, `epic_buried_p1`, `epic_low_leaves`, `jira_status_category`) | A correlated item informs another item's priority and unblocks, but an index-only bead never becomes a survey item (widening the survey was rejected).                                       | An `issue` or `pr` entity joined to a seed by a `jira`, `work`, `parent`, `mentions`, PR `depends_on` or external `references` link, in either direction, is a candidate; the reach is one hop and a linked-only candidate is never started.                                | RV-D (operator, 2026-10-08, second session).                                                       |
| Jira candidacy by assignee identity list (`operator_identities`)                                 | Jira items are whatever the Jira search returned; no assignee string is compared against a configured identity.                                                                              | A Jira issue is a seed when its assignee, trimmed of surrounding whitespace, equals one entry of `focus.operator_identities` exactly and case-sensitively; an empty list yields no Jira seeds and a notice, not a failure.                                                  | D-F23 (operator, 2026-10-08; the Jira half stands) and RV-E.                                       |
| Started tier from the Jira status category (`jira_status_category`, `headtohead`)                | No started tier: the ported suites order by due horizon, priority, unblocks and age, with every Jira item treated alike.                                                                     | A Jira seed is started when its status category is `indeterminate`; the category wins over the state name, and only when the snapshot carries none does a name in `jira.in_progress_statuses` decide (counted as `status_category_absent`).                                 | D-F11 (the started tier) and the Jira status category carried by the connector.                    |
| `blocked` is an open status (`blocked_open`)                                                     | The open-leaf walk of the epic suites counts `open` and `in_progress` leaves; their fixtures never create a blocked one.                                                                     | `open`, `in_progress` and `blocked` are the open statuses: a blocked bead can be a candidate and a blocked child is an open child that takes its epic's slot; a `deferred` bead is neither a candidate nor an open child.                                                   | The widened `blocked` open-beads query (operator, 2026-10-08) and R6.                              |
| Epic ranked by its top open leaf, a zero-leaf epic last (`epic_buried_p1`, `epic_low_leaves`)    | An epic is one row whose priority is its top open leaf priority; an epic with no open leaf is shown as `0 leaves`, ranked last and never put in the plan automatically.                      | An epic with an open direct child gives its slot to the child and is listed only in the trailing "epics with children in play" block; every open child that is a candidate ranks by its own keys.                                                                           | D-F11 slot rule (supersedes D-F7); no spec ruling beyond it was needed.                            |
| An epic with no open child ranks normally (`epic_zero_leaf`)                                     | The epic with zero open leaves ranks after every real item, even at priority P0, and is not in the plan.                                                                                     | The epic is a candidate in its own right and ranks by its own due, unblocks, priority and age, because the operator must move it along.                                                                                                                                     | D-F11 slot rule.                                                                                   |
| Age is the creation time (`age_tiebreak`)                                                        | The staler item by its last-updated time sorts first, so an item reorders whenever it is touched.                                                                                            | Age is the tracker's creation time, else the time pg-desk first stored the entity (every PR); the OLDEST item sorts first, and a fallback is counted as `age_fallback`.                                                                                                     | Operator ruling 2026-10-07 (spec, rank step, age key) and D-F5.                                    |
| Unblocks counts open direct blockers only (`unblocks_unavailable`, `headtohead`)                 | The count is bd's dependent count, which includes parent-child edges and closed children; an item with no bead correlation has a null count that sorts last.                                 | The count is the number of open DIRECT dependents joined by a `blocks` edge (a parent-child edge, a closed or inactive dependent does not count); an issue whose stored facts carry no issue dependencies counts 0 and is counted as `unblocks_unavailable`.                | D-F11 (the unblocks key) and the reverse-edge index of the rank step.                              |
| A non-positive cap is the default (`cap_zero`)                                                   | `--cap 0` defers everything: the plan starts empty.                                                                                                                                          | The rank treats a cap that is not positive as the default cap, 6; the rank itself never produces an empty plan. How a verb treats an explicit `--cap 0` belongs to the verb.                                                                                                | The rank as built; a recorded difference, not a spec ruling.                                       |
| Deployment-specific request-type floor dropped                                                   | Jira items of one deployment-specific request type (matched by a title prefix) are floored at priority P1 when they have none or a worse one, and a PR correlated to one inherits the floor. | No such rule: the priority of an item is its own mapped value (or the group's highest), never a floor by request type. The rule has no place in a public repository and needs its own bead if it is wanted.                                                                 | Not carried by the spec: dropped without a ruling; deployment-specific, so out of this repository. |
| Status phrase is not ranked or ported                                                            | `status_phrase` words a PR as merge-ready, blocked, draft, and so on, in the survey table.                                                                                                   | The rank has no such field; wording a PR state is a display concern of the `show` verb (its state column), so the phrase suite is not ported into the rank goldens.                                                                                                         | Not a rank input; the `show` packet owns the wording.                                              |

## Where each golden comes from

| Golden                                                 | Ported from                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `headtohead`, `headtohead_reversed`                    | The spec's evidence table (the operator's head-to-head rulings of 2026-10-05).         |
| `due_horizon`                                          | `test-df-survey-ranking.bats`, the due-horizon boundary test.                          |
| `priority_map`                                         | `test-df-survey-ranking.bats`, the priority mapping table.                             |
| `priority_inheritance`                                 | `test-df-survey-ranking.bats`, the correlated-priority tests.                          |
| `unblocks_unavailable`                                 | `test-df-survey-ranking.bats`, unblocks ordering and null handling.                    |
| `age_tiebreak`, `total_order_tiebreak`                 | `test-df-survey-ranking.bats`, the age and total-order tiebreak tests.                 |
| `cap_exact`, `cap_under`, `cap_default`, `cap_zero`    | `test-df-survey-cap.bats`.                                                             |
| `bd_due_timestamp`                                     | `test-df-survey-bd-fixtures.bats`, the due date read back as a midnight `Z` timestamp. |
| `epic_buried_p1`, `epic_low_leaves`, `epic_zero_leaf`  | `test-df-survey-epic-leaves.bats`.                                                     |
| `pr_candidates`, `operator_identities`, `blocked_open` | The candidate rules (D-F2, D-F23, RV-C, RV-D) the suites above did not need to state.  |
| `jira_status_category`                                 | The Jira status category rule; df-survey had no started tier.                          |

## Fixture format

One JSON object per file; see the header of `rank_golden_test.go` for the fields. The expected block
names the rank order, the tier of every row, the deciding key under every row but the last, the epics
in play and the five `rank_inputs` counts; `priorities`, `due` and `in_plan` are optional extra
assertions. A fixture whose expectation does not cover the whole ranking is rejected by the harness.
